Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business outlets is dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's ouster as Nvidia CEO, including a growing campaign to reinstate him and intensifying Washington scrutiny of chip exports to China, alongside intense focus on Anthropic's imminent blockbuster IPO as a test of the broader AI trade's health.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang discusses a comeback as Nvidia CEO, igniting a 'war room' campaign
stories.summary: The FT reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been discussing a possible return with allies, who have formed a lobbying effort; Fortune describes allies assembling a 'war room' with a petition that had topped 175,000 signatures including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney and Travis Kalanick, while Treasury Secretary Bessent has pushed for an outside successor and questioned whether Nvidia broke the law on China sales.

stories.headline: Anthropic's mega-IPO becomes a referendum on the AI trade
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports bankers expect to price Anthropic's potentially record-breaking IPO on Wednesday with trading starting Thursday, framing it as reassurance for investors that the AI trade will endure under new de facto industry leader Dario Amodei now that Huang is out at Nvidia; WSJ and Axios note Nvidia and sovereign-wealth funds stand to win big, while Fortune reports the offering values Anthropic up to $1.4 trillion, well below earlier $2 trillion hopes.

stories.headline: Congress presses Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Lutnick over China chip exports
stories.summary: Puck reports newly emboldened Democrats, who take control of Congress in January, are demanding to know what the White House knew about Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy and Nvidia's chip sales in Asia, with Huang agreeing to testify on Capitol Hill; the Washington Post separately reports Republican criticism of Commerce Secretary Lutnick has grown over his inaction on export curbs.

stories.headline: Trump's personal Nvidia stake surged to $62 million before scandal broke
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports that President Trump's financial disclosures show his Nvidia holdings rose sharply as his administration eased rules letting the chipmaker sell advanced chips in China, benefiting him personally as the company's China sales came under scrutiny.

stories.headline: Tech stocks tumble again as Nvidia leadership drama and Anthropic IPO collide
stories.summary: The WSJ reports Nvidia stock was set to drop further and tech futures slumped as the ongoing Huang leadership saga collided with this week's high-stakes Anthropic IPO test for the AI trade; Bloomberg similarly reports a selloff carried into the new week as traders cut risk ahead of Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's debut.

stories.headline: Gucci cuts prices as luxury demand weakens, while Louis Vuitton resists
stories.summary: The WSJ reports that with luxury demand weak, Gucci has begun cutting prices while Louis Vuitton executives are debating whether to break one of the sector's long-standing taboos and follow suit.

stories.headline: Microsoft says all services restored after global outage hit hospitals, police
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports Microsoft completed efforts to fix a global outage that had disrupted communications at government services, hospitals, and police departments worldwide.

stories.headline: Dangote invests $2.2 billion to upgrade Nigeria's road network
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, is spending 3.3 trillion naira ($2.2 billion) through his businesses to upgrade Nigeria's road network to ease transport of goods.

Business.gaps: Business Insider had no identifiable recent business-relevant coverage in the feed or accessible search results; Politico's business-relevant item was limited to midterm political coverage of the GOP rather than core business news.

US politics.overview: Outlets are dominated by three intertwined stories: a rare, contested Senate Democratic leadership fight between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen; the fallout and funding fight from Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop; and President Trump's Asia trip to meet Xi and Putin just as the Nvidia/Jensen Huang scandal roils Washington. Midterm post-mortems and intra-party debates (GOP's MAGA direction, Democrats' agenda) also feature heavily across opinion and news pages.

stories.headline: Van Hollen's challenge to Schumer exposes Democratic rifts ahead of Dec. 1 vote
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, with Axios reporting the race exposes divisions within the party days after its sweeping midterm victory, with Schumer holding more public endorsements but Van Hollen claiming growing momentum ahead of the Dec. 1 secret-ballot vote.

stories.headline: FAA ground stop ignites fight over $50 billion aviation funding request
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is pushing Congress for an emergency $50 billion to modernize air traffic control after Friday's nationwide ground stop, but Democrats led by Rosa DeLauro are skeptical, noting the department hasn't spent billions already appropriated, adding a new complication to the Dec. 11 government funding deadline.

stories.headline: Trump heads to Asia to meet Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
stories.summary: Trump's second China trip of the year comes as his administration faces backlash from midterm losses, with the Nvidia espionage and personal scandal surrounding founder Jensen Huang threatening to overshadow the diplomacy.

stories.headline: Nvidia scandal deepens as Trump's personal stake and Huang's fate draw scrutiny
stories.summary: Financial disclosures show the value of Trump's Nvidia holdings rose to as much as $62 million before an espionage and extramarital-affair scandal involving founder Jensen Huang broke, even as Silicon Valley figures reportedly push for Huang's reinstatement and the administration remains divided over how to respond.

stories.headline: Poll finds Republicans split on party direction after midterm losses
stories.summary: A new POLITICO poll finds tension within the GOP over where to go next after a decade of unity around Trump, revealing cracks in the MAGA coalition following the party's midterm defeat.

stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear case on Trump's asylum suspension policy
stories.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to decide whether the Trump administration can suspend access to asylum for migrants at the U.S.-Mexico border, after a D.C. Circuit panel ruled the policy exceeded the executive's removal authority under federal immigration law.

stories.headline: Pentagon builds its own case against general accused of leaking
stories.summary: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia faces legal jeopardy on two fronts after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's team's leak allegations were referred to the Justice Department, with the Pentagon now preparing its own prosecution.

stories.headline: Democrats weigh immigration reform options and DHS oversight push ahead of taking control
stories.summary: Democrats are exploring ways to rein in Trump's mass deportation operations once they retake Congress, though the party remains split on how far to go, as a Democrat eyeing a Homeland Security oversight gavel vows to "dismantle DHS from the inside."

US politics.gaps: NOTUS's available content was more than 90 days old with nothing from the last 48 hours surfacing in search; Cook Political Report had no recent coverage found. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian entries are limited to the specific feed items provided since these outlets block general web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid an alleged Chinese espionage affair, with ripple effects into chip export policy, Nvidia's stock, and a Silicon Valley campaign to reinstate him. The other major storyline is Anthropic's imminent blockbuster IPO, landing amid a broader bout of AI-stock volatility that has outlets questioning whether the 'AI trade' is cracking.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit spirals into a full-blown corporate crisis
stories.summary: Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed a return as Nvidia CEO with allies who are assembling a Silicon Valley 'war room' to lobby the board, even as Treasury Secretary Bessent pushes the board to pick an outsider instead.

stories.headline: Firm tied to Huang's alleged affair brokered billions in Nvidia chip sales to China
stories.summary: Megaspeed, the firm owned by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of Jensen Huang's ousting, reportedly arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, fueling new congressional pushes to tighten AI chip export rules.

stories.headline: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO lands amid deep uncertainty
stories.summary: Days before what could be the largest IPO in history, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying enough compute "the deepest business dilemma" the company faces, with commitments now totaling nearly $901 billion.

stories.headline: Tech stocks slide as 'AI trade' faces its biggest test yet
stories.summary: A selloff in technology stocks extended into a new week as traders moved to cut risk ahead of Nvidia's high-stakes earnings and Anthropic's expected market debut.

stories.headline: Amazon's Zoox robotaxis go live on Uber in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Amazon-owned Zoox has partnered with Uber for the first time, letting riders in Las Vegas be matched with its purpose-built robotaxis through the Uber app.

stories.headline: ULA's Vulcan rocket suffers first-ever mission failure, destroying 40 Amazon satellites
stories.summary: United Launch Alliance suffered what is reportedly its first total mission failure in 20 years, destroying 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo broadband constellation, a competitor to SpaceX's Starlink.

stories.headline: AI cheating scandal rattles South Korea's national exam system
stories.summary: South Korea's top scorer on a national exam has admitted to using AI to answer 160 of 161 questions correctly by photographing and sending them to an AI tool, raising fears ahead of next week's college entrance exam.

Tech & AI.gaps: VentureBeat and Google DeepMind had no recent AI-related items surfaced in search; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were only covered via the provided feed items since they block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, where negotiators are wrestling with a stalled electrification pledge and a sharp drop in climate-finance commitments, alongside a wave of oil and gas M&A and fresh economic signals on energy prices. Trade press like Heatmap and Canary Media are also tracking drought-hit US hydropower, state-level clean energy policy after the midterms, and new clean-tech financing deals.

stories.headline: Push to Electrify the Global Economy Stalls at UN Climate Talks
stories.summary: A bid by COP31 hosts to get nearly 200 nations to back a pledge raising electricity's share of global energy demand to 35% by 2035 is running into resistance during the Antalya negotiations, according to Bloomberg, which notes the figure is just over 20% currently.

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's own analysis found that public climate-finance pledges from rich nations for the coming years have dropped more than 70% compared with 2025 levels, with Germany, France, Japan and the US notably absent from new commitments, a shortfall that is fueling friction among delegates at the summit.

stories.headline: Canadian Natural to Buy Advantage Energy Amid Oil Price Boom
stories.summary: Canadian Natural Resources agreed to acquire smaller rival Advantage Energy for about C$2.53 billion including debt, part of a string of Canadian oil and gas deals as Middle East and Ukraine conflicts boost demand for alternative crude supplies.

stories.headline: Diamondback Agrees to Buy Parts of Shale Producer Double Eagle
stories.summary: Diamondback Energy agreed to buy certain subsidiaries of Double Eagle for $2.15 billion in cash and stock, a deal expected to add roughly 35,000 barrels a day to its Permian Basin production in 2027.

stories.headline: European Gas Dips as Record US Flows Counter Storage Concerns
stories.summary: European natural gas prices fell as traders balanced record US export flows against ongoing worries about thin winter storage inventories across the continent.

stories.headline: Hydropower Is Drying up in the American West
stories.summary: Hydropower generation in the US Southwest hit a record low this summer as prolonged Colorado River Basin drought cut electricity output 19% below last year and 28% below the 10-year average, per new EIA data cited by Heatmap.

stories.headline: A year in, New England heat pump program is thriving
stories.summary: More than 25,000 New England homes have installed federally-funded, energy-efficient heat pump systems through a five-state accelerator program that launched a year ago, with backers confident it can hit its goal of 580,000 installations in four years.

stories.headline: Bedrock Energy Raises $24 Million to Mainstream Small-Scale Geothermal
stories.summary: Texas startup Bedrock Energy raised $24 million to use AI and sensors to drill fewer, deeper and cheaper geothermal wells for home and building HVAC, a technology that currently serves only about 1% of single-family homes.

Energy.gaps: Latitude Media, E&E News, and Argus Media had no clearly recent (last 24-48h) coverage surfaced in search; older E&E material from earlier in the year was excluded as outdated. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT, and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items provided for this group, so their current coverage could not be assessed beyond the unrelated WSJ tech items in the feed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese state media, regional outlets and global wires is dominated by this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen and the unprecedented Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting, alongside fresh signs of a soft patch in China's domestic economy even as tech exports and AI model releases surge. Business coverage is focused on fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's scandal and its implications for the US-China chip race, plus routine but telling moves in EVs, steel and monetary policy.

stories.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin to hold first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry confirmed that Xi Jinping will hold a historic China-Russia-US summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on November 19, described by Beijing as the first-ever face-to-face meeting among the three countries' top leaders. State-run Xinhua and Global Times frame the meeting as proof of China's role as a 'stable and responsible major country,' while Western outlets note Trump wants to discuss nuclear arms reduction but not Ukraine.

stories.headline: China's factory output and retail sales slow as domestic demand sags
stories.summary: China's October data showed retail sales growth slowing to just 0.4% as a prolonged property crisis keeps household spending subdued, even as technology exports stay strong, underscoring that policymakers are holding back from broad stimulus. WSJ separately noted that while demand for Chinese goods abroad is soaring, domestic consumption and investment momentum keep weakening, leaving growth reliant on exports.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback bid tests US-China chip politics
stories.summary: Tech industry allies are lobbying Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang after he resigned following revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, while Treasury Secretary Bessent has separately urged the chipmaker to pick an outsider as the next CEO. SCMP reported that many Chinese Nvidia employees are staying on the sidelines of a petition campaign to bring Huang back despite more than 170,000 signatures.

stories.headline: China's central bank raises foreign exchange reserve requirement for first time in 5 years
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China raised the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio for financial institutions to 6% from 4%, a move aimed at curbing yuan appreciation that could otherwise squeeze exporters.

stories.headline: Chinese AI giants race out new models as DeepSeek hits capacity limits
stories.summary: Tencent launched a cheaper Hy4 flash AI model, Alibaba made its flagship Qwen4-Max generally available with a million-token context window, and Huawei Cloud previewed an open-source robotics world model, even as DeepSeek users reported new usage caps that the company attributed to capacity constraints.

stories.headline: China's steel mills brace for a bitter winter amid overcapacity
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that struggling Chinese steel producers face a renewed threat of closures this winter as years of overproduction continue to weigh on the sector.

stories.headline: Hong Kong police switch on facial recognition across AI-enabled CCTV network
stories.summary: Hong Kong police began activating facial recognition tools across their surveillance camera system as part of a HK$4 billion plan, with the police chief insisting the tools 'won't be abused.'

stories.headline: Beijing tightens oversight of automaker supplier payments
stories.summary: Chinese regulators will require 17 automakers, including BYD, Nio and Xiaomi, to submit supplier payment reports for 2026 and the fourth quarter by January 31, 2027, as the basis for a first formal assessment of payment practices.

China.gaps: Could not find distinct recent coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global (beyond an older Tencent layoff fact-check), or China Daily within the last 48 hours; Reuters and AP blocked web search and had no relevant feed items provided; The Economist and NYT had no relevant feed items provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the renewed Iran-Bahrain military escalation, with Iranian drone strikes on a US radar base triggering nationwide alerts, Gulf-wide condemnation and a third US aircraft carrier deploying to the region. Diplomatic coverage centers on US envoy Mike Waltz's Beirut visit to negotiate what replaces UNIFIL and pressure Hezbollah to disarm, while business desks track UAE fiscal resilience and Jordan's economic positioning amid regional shocks.

stories.headline: Iran attacks Bahrain again, Gulf states condemn 'blatant challenge' to peace push
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired six drones at a US radar installation at Bahrain's Riffa airbase in the second such attack within a week, with Bahrain's military saying all were intercepted; the GCC, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar condemned the strikes as a serious escalation. The IRGC also claimed oil tankers were hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claims that remain unverified.

stories.headline: US envoy Waltz presses Lebanon on Hezbollah disarmament as UNIFIL withdrawal looms
stories.summary: US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz met Lebanon's president, PM and parliament speaker in Beirut to discuss a replacement for UNIFIL, whose mandate expires in December, while insisting Hezbollah must disarm 'voluntarily' since no country can have two armies. Israel has reportedly rejected Lebanon's proposals for a multinational monitoring force, leaving the post-UNIFIL security arrangement unresolved.

stories.headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has joined two other US carriers already deployed to the Middle East as Washington and Israel weigh further action against Iran, a build-up that coincides with Iran's renewed drone attacks on Bahrain.

stories.headline: US intelligence says Iran still holds up to 2,500 missiles, contradicting Trump
stories.summary: New US intelligence estimates show Iran has rebuilt a missile stockpile of up to 2,500, undercutting earlier claims from the Trump administration that Tehran's arsenal was nearly depleted and feeding into debate over resuming strikes.

stories.headline: UAE budget to stay in surplus in 2026 despite war-related spending surge, Fitch says
stories.summary: Fitch Ratings affirmed the UAE at AA- with a stable outlook, projecting the consolidated budget will hold a 4% of GDP surplus even as spending jumped nearly 20% to offset the impact of the regional war, while GDP growth is forecast at just 0.5% for the year.

stories.headline: Jordan set to thrive amid regional shocks, EU diplomat says
stories.summary: An EU diplomat told The National that Jordan's economy, anchored by Aqaba's port and trade links, is positioned to benefit even as regional conflict disrupts neighboring markets.

stories.headline: Jordan and Iraq both ban Telegram over security and content concerns
stories.summary: Jordan announced a ban on Telegram, accusing the platform of fueling extremism, a move made within hours of Iraq separately banning the app for failing to meet local legal and regulatory requirements.

stories.headline: Netanyahu secretly met informant before election in alleged voter fraud scheme
stories.summary: A new report alleges Netanyahu held a secret pre-election meeting with an informant to launch a voter fraud operation, amid multiple arrests over related fraud and bribery allegations.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not independently verify current coverage from Gulf News beyond the Bahrain/Iran live blogs, Haaretz, Ynetnews, Iran International, AGBI, Arabian Business, Zawya, Al Jazeera, Saudi Gazette or The New Arab within the last 24-48 hours; items shown from Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC were limited to what appeared in the provided feed.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by big corporate and investment moves out of Nigeria, DRC and South Africa, alongside security and geopolitical stories from South Africa, Sudan and Ethiopia. Business and economy outlets (TechCabal, Bloomberg, The Africa Report, Mining Weekly) are tracking major deals in telecoms, cobalt, roads and stock exchanges, while Africanews leads on violent crime and Horn of Africa tensions.

stories.headline: DRC finance minister on cobalt pricing power and debut bond
stories.summary: DRC finance minister Doudou Fwamba discusses Kinshasa's first international bond, cobalt export quotas, and efforts to attract investment despite ongoing war and an Ebola outbreak.

stories.headline: Dangote invests $2.2 billion to upgrade Nigeria's road network
stories.summary: Africa's richest man Aliko Dangote says his businesses are spending roughly 3.3 trillion naira to upgrade Nigeria's road network to ease transport of goods.

stories.headline: MTN reopens talks to acquire Telkom
stories.summary: MTN has restarted acquisition talks with South African operator Telkom four years after a previous takeover attempt collapsed, with Telkom's valuation now nearly double what it was then.

stories.headline: 17 killed in two mass shootings as South Africa battles rising violent crime
stories.summary: Seventeen people were killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, including nine victims found shot dead inside a shack near Pretoria, underscoring the country's persistent violent crime problem.

stories.headline: Sudan and Ethiopia trade accusations over armed groups
stories.summary: Tensions between Khartoum and Addis Ababa have escalated as each government accuses the other of backing armed groups fighting within its borders, complicating regional conflict-resolution efforts.

stories.headline: NGX Group expands into East Africa with 10% stake in Nairobi bourse
stories.summary: The Nigerian Exchange Group has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange as part of a broader pan-African growth strategy.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers under Anglo's proposed exit
stories.summary: Angola's mines ministry is seeking a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's planned sale of its stake in the diamond producer, according to a Reuters report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Web Summit 2026: Africa seeks bigger role as China steals the show
stories.summary: At Web Summit in Lisbon, African startups pushed for investment and international partnerships even as China's displays of AI and robotics dominated attention.

Africa.gaps: Africa Confidential's most recent dated items were from November 6-11, outside the 24-48 hour window, so no current lead story could be confirmed. The Continent's available editions in search results were from August/September 2026, so nothing recent was found. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block search and had no relevant feed items provided, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past 24-48 hours centers on upheaval inside legacy TV news (CBS, CNN, MS NOW/NBC), fresh scrutiny of Bari Weiss's media properties, and press-freedom flashpoints involving the Trump administration and the FCC. Trade outlets are also tracking business-model shifts—AI licensing, creator-economy plays, and one media company's aggressive hiring spree—while entertainment trades converge on a wave of TV staffing news.

stories.headline: CBS News and CNN see exodus of staff amid Skydance/Paramount ownership shake-up
stories.summary: Status reports that Skydance's buyout offers at CNN and CBS News are triggering a wave of veteran staff departures, including "Face the Nation" boss Mary Hager leaving CBS News, with irate staffers reportedly accusing network brass of throwing journalists under the bus after the administration's attacks on a '60 Minutes' report.

stories.headline: Willie Geist to leave 'Morning Joe' after nearly 20 years for expanded NBC 'Today' role
stories.summary: Willie Geist will focus full-time on NBC News' Sunday Today and expand his presence on Today, departing MS NOW's Morning Joe at year's end after serving as the last remaining on-air talent shared by NBC News and MS NOW since their split.

stories.headline: Trump administration, via Stephen Miller, pursues a national security journalist's 'scalp'
stories.summary: CJR examines whether White House aide Stephen Miller will help deliver Donald Trump a high-profile takedown of a national security journalist, part of the administration's ongoing pressure campaign on the press.

stories.headline: Reporters Without Borders calls for impeachment of FCC Chair Brendan Carr
stories.summary: In an unprecedented move, the press freedom group RSF has for the first time called for the impeachment of a sitting U.S. official, citing what it calls the severity and persistence of FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's misconduct and the need to restore the commission's independence.

stories.headline: Scrutiny mounts over editorial standards at Bari Weiss's Free Press
stories.summary: Status reports that an AI-altered photo, a retracted video, and a quietly shelved interview have raised fresh questions about editorial standards at The Free Press, the Bari Weiss-founded outlet separate from her role atop CBS News.

stories.headline: The Atlantic's aggressive hiring spree raises questions about its business strategy
stories.summary: Puck reports The Atlantic has made at least 18 new editorial hires in six months, fueling debate over whether owner Laurene Powell Jobs's spending reflects sound strategy or the luxury of an owner unmotivated by profit.

stories.headline: Eurovision organizers criticize Malaysian broadcaster over cut LGBT+ footage
stories.summary: Eurovision's organizers said they were surprised and disappointed that broadcaster TV3 appeared to cut footage of Thai drag performers and a gay Philippine jury spokesperson during the first Eurovision Asia contest.

stories.headline: Hearst launches Creator Studios, structured like a talent agency
stories.summary: Hearst Magazines has debuted a creator-focused unit with 50 editor-selected creators and original series, signaling legacy publishers' deepening push into the creator economy alongside brand deals that could reach seven figures.

Media.gaps: WSJ, FT, and Bloomberg had no media-industry-specific items surfaced in the feed or accessible search for this period; coverage from NYT and WSJ on this topic could not be independently verified beyond what appeared in other outlets' references to them.
